title: FreeTimeGS: Free Gaussian Primitives at Anytime and Anywhere for Dynamic Scene Reconstruction
tldr: Let a Gaussian be born at any time and place instead of deforming a canonical one, and complex motion stops breaking 4D reconstruction.

problem.task: Reconstruct a dynamic 3D scene and render novel views at novel times.

inputs.name: multi-view video
inputs.chars: Synchronized rigs; scenes with fast and complex motion.

outputs.name: 4D Gaussians
outputs.chars: Each primitive carries a lifespan and a motion function, so it moves rather than being warped.

training.note: Motion functions cut temporal redundancy, which is where the efficiency comes from.

method.intuition: Canonical-space deformation fields are hard to optimize when the motion is large, so drop the canonical space and let primitives live where and when the motion actually is.

experiments.headline: Rendering quality above recent methods by a large margin on several dynamic-scene datasets.

why: The current answer to capturing a physical scene while it is being changed, which every digital-twin pipeline needs.

title: MetaScenes: Towards Automated Replica Creation for Real-world 3D Scans
tldr: Simulatable scenes have been artist-built and therefore scarce. Scan a real room, auto-replace every object with a matched simulatable asset, and the scarcity goes away.

problem.task: Turn a real-world 3D scan into an interactive simulatable replica without an artist.

outputs.name: simulatable scene
outputs.chars: 15,366 objects across 831 fine-grained categories, each replaced by a matched asset.

training.supervision: Scan2Sim is a multi-modal alignment model trained to pick the right asset for each scanned object.
training.note: The bottleneck it removes is human labour, so the contribution is a pipeline as much as a dataset.

method.intuition: Embodied AI needs the diversity of the real world in a form physics can act on, and only automation gets both.

experiments.headline: Supports more generalizable agent learning and better sim-to-real alignment than artist-built alternatives.

why: Bridges the geometry papers above and the simulator papers below: reconstruction is only useful once it is actionable.

title: Video World Models with Long-term Spatial Memory
tldr: A video world model forgets the room the moment it leaves it. Give it a geometry-grounded memory to write to and read from, and revisits stay consistent.

problem.task: Long-horizon action-conditioned video generation that stays consistent when the camera returns somewhere it has been.

inputs.name: past frames
inputs.chars: Bounded by the model's context window, which is the failure this addresses.

inputs.name: spatial memory
inputs.chars: Geometry-grounded store of what was generated earlier.

training.supervision: Custom curated datasets built for training and evaluating explicit 3D memory.
training.note: Memory is stored in geometry rather than in tokens, which is why revisits align rather than merely rhyme.

method.intuition: Forgetting in world models is a storage problem, not a capacity problem, and geometry is the natural index for a physical scene.

experiments.headline: Better quality, consistency and usable context length than baselines on long-horizon world generation.

why: Names the specific reason generative world models cannot yet stand in for a persistent physical environment.

title: Reconstructing and grounding narrated instructional videos in 3D
tldr: Different YouTube videos of the same car engine are different instances of one object. Reconstruct it across videos and the narration lands on a 3D part.

problem.task: Reconstruct an object class in 3D from many unaligned instructional videos, then ground the narration to it.

inputs.name: instructional videos
inputs.chars: Different products, lighting and versions of the same object — the reason instance-level SfM fails.

inputs.name: narration
inputs.chars: Free speech, wide variation in phrasing.

outputs.name: 3D reconstruction
outputs.chars: Aligned across videos through a 3D alignment graph.

training.supervision: None. Raw videos, no manual annotation.
training.note: Divide-and-conquer: reconstruct per video first, then align the reconstructions.

method.intuition: Instructional video is a giant uncalibrated multi-view capture of the world's objects, if you can match across instances rather than across frames.
method.backbone: learnt local features + dense flow + SfM
components: two-step reconstruction with a 3D alignment graph

experiments.headline: Reconstructs engines of different car models from raw video with no manual supervision and associates the narration with 3D regions.

why: An early and still-underused idea: instructional video is 3D data about the physical world, on top of being a sequence of steps.

title: Towards World Simulator: Crafting Physical Commonsense-Based Benchmark for Video Generation
tldr: 160 prompts across 27 physical laws, plus an automatic grader that agrees with humans, and current text-to-video models fail most of them.

problem.task: Score whether a generated video obeys physical commonsense.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.chars: 160 prompts covering 27 physical laws in four domains.

outputs.name: physics correctness score
outputs.chars: From PhyGenEval, a hierarchical VLM and LLM grader calibrated against human judgment.

training.note: The grader is the reusable part — a physics score you can run at scale rather than by eye.

method.intuition: If video generators are world simulators, intuitive physics is the thing to measure, and nobody was measuring it.

experiments.headline: Current models struggle to obey physical commonsense, and neither scaling the model nor prompt engineering closes the gap.

why: The measurement that keeps the generative world-model claim honest.

title: Assessing Adaptive World Models in Machines with Novel Games
tldr: Current world-model evaluation scores a representation learned from a giant corpus. The human capacity worth measuring is building a new one fast, inside an environment you have never seen.

problem.task: Evaluate world model induction — how efficiently an agent builds a usable model of a genuinely novel environment.

inputs.name: novel game
inputs.chars: Deep, continually refreshing novelty in the underlying rules, so memorization cannot help.

outputs.name: induced model + policy
outputs.chars: Scored on efficiency of adaptation rather than final performance.

training.supervision: A position paper with a proposed benchmarking paradigm.
training.note: The desiderata for what counts as a novel game are the operational contribution.

method.intuition: Adaptability comes from constructing and refining an internal model quickly, so evaluate the construction rather than the artifact.
components: world model induction framing from cognitive science

why: The sharpest available critique of how this list's world-model papers are currently evaluated.

title: HUMOTO: A 4D Dataset of Mocap Human Object Interactions
tldr: 735 mocap sequences of whole-body interaction with 63 modelled objects and 72 articulated parts, scripted by an LLM so the tasks have a purpose rather than a pose list.

problem.task: High-fidelity 4D human-object interaction capture for motion generation, vision and robotics.

inputs.name: task script
inputs.chars: Scene-driven, LLM-authored, with natural task progression rather than isolated actions.

outputs.name: object poses
outputs.chars: 63 modelled objects, 72 articulated parts, simultaneous multi-object interaction.

training.supervision: Marker-based motion capture plus camera, cleaned and verified by professional artists.
training.note: Artist cleanup targets foot sliding and object penetration, which is what makes it usable as physics supervision.

method.intuition: Interaction datasets are usually a list of isolated grasps. Scripting complete purposeful tasks keeps the logical flow that makes the motion realistic.
components: mocap plus camera setup handling occlusion

experiments.headline: 735 sequences with simultaneous multi-object interaction and full-body motion, benchmarked against existing HOI datasets.

why: The measurement ground for whole-body interaction, which sits between the hand-object papers and the humanoid ones.

title: Mask2IV: Interaction-Centric Video Generation via Mask Trajectories
tldr: Mask control makes interaction video better but nobody has dense masks. Predict the actor and object trajectories first, then generate conditioned on those.

problem.task: Generate video of a human or robot interacting with a named object, controllable without dense mask input.

inputs.name: control
inputs.tensor: target object + action description or position cue
inputs.chars: Users specify what to interact with and roughly how, not a per-frame mask.

outputs.name: interaction video
outputs.chars: Conditioned on predicted actor and object mask trajectories.

training.supervision: Two stages trained separately: trajectory prediction, then trajectory-conditioned generation.
training.note: Decoupling is what removes the dense-annotation dependency at inference.

method.intuition: The mask trajectory is the useful control signal, so predict it rather than asking a user to draw it.

baselines: mask-conditioned and text-conditioned interaction video generation
experiments.headline: Removes the dense-mask requirement while keeping control over the target object and the motion.

why: Interaction video is where robot learning gets its visual priors, so how it is controlled matters downstream.

title: Egocentric Human-Object Interaction Detection: A New Benchmark and Method
tldr: Third-person HOI detectors collapse from a head-mounted camera, where the hand occludes the object it is holding. 27K annotated egocentric images and a hand-geometry fix.

problem.task: Detect hand-verb-object triplets from a first-person image.

inputs.name: egocentric image
inputs.chars: 27K images, 123 interaction categories, single- and two-hand.

training.supervision: Manual triplet annotation across diverse daily scenarios.
training.note: HGIR is plug-and-play, so the gain can be attributed to the hand-geometry cue rather than to a new architecture.

method.intuition: The egocentric difficulty is hand-object occlusion, and the hand's own pose is the cue that survives it.
method.backbone: HOI detector + Hand Geometry and Interactivity Refinement
components: global hand geometric features from pose proposals

experiments.headline: Large performance gaps for third-person detectors on egocentric input, closed substantially by the hand-geometry refinement.

why: Quantifies how much of third-person perception simply does not transfer to the viewpoint a wearable actually has.

title: Universal Visuo-Tactile Video Understanding for Embodied Interaction
tldr: Hardness, elasticity and friction are invisible. 150K frames across three tactile sensors, aligned to language, so a model can say what a surface feels like.

problem.task: Answer questions about physical attributes from tactile video.

inputs.name: visuo-tactile video
inputs.chars: From GelSight Mini, DIGIT or Tac3D — cross-sensor by construction.

outputs.name: tactile description
outputs.chars: Grounded in hardness, protrusion, elasticity and friction.

training.supervision: VTV150K: 150,000 frames from 100 objects, annotated with four tactile attributes.
training.note: Three-stage training — representation, cross-modal alignment, then prompt fine-tuning.

method.intuition: Vision and language cannot recover the physical attributes that only contact reveals, so the tactile stream has to enter the model rather than sit beside it.

experiments.headline: The first multi-modal LLM for universal visuo-tactile video understanding, spanning three different tactile sensors.

why: The one sensing channel on this list that no camera substitutes for, and the axis most of the field still ignores.

title: Ego-R1: Chain-of-Tool-Thought for Ultra-Long Egocentric Video Reasoning
tldr: A week of first-person video does not fit in any context window, so train an RL agent to call one retrieval tool per reasoning step instead.

problem.task: Question answering over egocentric video spanning days to weeks.

inputs.name: ultra-long egocentric video
inputs.chars: Week-long recordings; no model ingests this directly.

outputs.name: tool call sequence
outputs.chars: One tool per step — temporal retrieval, multimodal understanding.

training.supervision: SFT on Ego-CoTT-25K, then RL on Ego-QA-4.4K.
training.note: The agent decides which tool to call, so the context problem becomes a policy problem.

method.intuition: Long-context reasoning over a life is retrieval scheduling, and scheduling is something an RL agent can learn.

experiments.headline: Tool-augmented chain-of-thought handles ultra-long egocentric reasoning where direct long-context models do not.

why: Pushes the temporal horizon of this list from a clip to a life, which is the scale a wearable assistant actually operates at.
